doc:
The lambda(U) route at l=3, k <= 6: distil T (or CS, CCZ) states with the distance-2 factories of the catalogue, then convert them into the target with Clifford gates, Pauli measurements and feedforward, no catalysts; against our factory. lambda(U) = fewest |T> states from which stabilizer operations (Cliffords, Pauli measurements, feedforward) make |U>, without catalysts. lambda(U) <= tau(U) (CNOT+T synthesis). What we use from Beverland, Campbell, Howard, Kliuchnikov, arXiv:1904.01124 (full text read): (a) stabilizer nullity nu is monotone under stabilizer operations, measurements included, and additive (Sec. 2.1, Prop. 4.1), so lambda(U) >= nu(U). We compute nu exactly (Pauli spectrum, searches/full_clifford_classes.py). (b) stabilizer extent xi is monotone under stabilizer operations (Sec. 1.1, 2.2) and multiplicative on products of states of at most three qubits (Lemma 2.7(1)). Hence m T states make |psi> only if m >= log xi(psi) / log xi(T); Table 1 gives this ratio as 2.96818 for CS and 3.63356 for CCZ (W3: 3.63356, W4: 4.99907, W5: 5.93637). For a product of T, CS, CCZ on disjoint qubits, xi multiplies (each factor has <= 3 qubits), so lambda >= ceil(a + 2.96818 b + 3.63356 c). The asterisk of Table 1 ("not known to hold for arbitrary catalysts") does not apply: we exclude catalysts, and the inputs T^m are products of 1-qubit states. For W4, W5 the extent itself is "computed to eight digits and reconstructed", not proved (App. A.4); those rows are flagged. (c) upper bounds without catalysts: tau(U) (exact T-count, staged_best 'tau'), minimized over the full-Clifford class (outputs/checks/full_clifford_classes.json): Clifford gates are free on this route. 4 T -> CCZ (Jones, [32] of Table 1) is tau of CS01,CS02, a member of the CCZ class, so it is covered by this minimum. For products of T, CS, CCZ on disjoint qubits also a + 3b + 4c (one T, three T for CS, four for CCZ, each without catalyst). lambda is called known for a class when the best lower bound equals the best upper bound. Route cost at distance 2: the fewest inputs for lambda T states from the cheapest distance-2 T^m factories of the catalogue (outputs/large_unified_factories.csv, rows d=2 whose output is a product of T gates), batched; for products, also any mix of directly distilled CS and CCZ states (pure CS^m, CCZ^m factories of the same catalogue) and T states for the rest. To first order the error of the route is the sum over the distilled states, so it is a distance-2 route. T supply, strongest distance-2 alternative we know besides the catalogue: Meier, Eastin, Knill, arXiv:1204.4221 (full text read, Sec. II-III): the four-qubit-code routine takes ten |H> states to two, accepts with a(p) = 1 - 10p + O(p^2), output error u(p) = 9p^2 + O(p^3) per output (every single error detected), no catalyst. |H> = cos(pi/8)|0> + sin(pi/8)|1> is Clifford-equivalent to |T> = T|+> (checked numerically below), so it is a T^2 factory with n = 10 for this route. Every T count below is the cheapest batching of the catalogue T^m factories and MEK (10 inputs per 2 T states, surplus discarded). The CS and CCZ pieces use the cheaper of the catalogue pure factories and T states (3 T per CS, 4 T per CCZ) from that supply. Added 2026-11-06 (referee round 4), from Balada Gaggioli and Marecek, arXiv:2610.31115 (full text read): (i) Prop. 7 and Table I, a nine-input distance-2 factory for one T state (acceptance 1/128, error 27/2 p^2), and Prop. 5, no stabilizer protocol does it with eight, so T^1 costs 9 here per run; per accepted output it costs more (that paper, Discussion: "per accepted output, the nine-input T factory consumes more inputs than the ten-input protocol"), while the other factories used accept with 1 - n p + O(p^2). The tallies are therefore also reported without it (tally_without_BGM, tally_full_clifford_without_BGM); (ii) Prop. 10 (= Beverland et al. Prop. A.4): projecting one qubit of |CCZ> onto (|0> +- i|1>)/sqrt2 leaves CS|++> up to a Clifford, so m CS states cost at most what m CCZ states cost (8 for one, [[8,3,2]]; Table I: n_min(CS,2) = 8). Both are measurement routes without catalysts and are used for the T and CS pieces below (checked: cs_from_ccz_check); the CS and CCZ pieces may also be drawn together from one batch of CCZ states (CCZ^m factories of the catalogue). Full-Clifford groups are read from outputs/checks/full_clifford_classes.json; member labels are 'k:orbit:spec' and the k=6 orbit labels contain colons ('6:0:1536:CCZ045,CCZ123'), so the orbit is everything between the first and last colon. Invariants reported for the full-Clifford classes (all exact Clifford invariants, see invariants()): Pauli spectrum (multiset of |

|), the number of Lagrangians inside the zero set, and the multiset of per-label Lagrangian counts. Also recounted for every class: the nullity floor LB(nu) of outputs/nullity_l3.json (cheapest T/CS/CCZ supply of total nullity >= nu; a lower bound for every such route, measurements included). python searches/lambda_route.py -> outputs/checks/lambda_route.{json,md}

invariants.note: each count of distinct values is a lower bound on the number of full-Clifford classes; the exact count (union of label sets, full_clifford_classes.json) is the number of groups
